definition: The short, catchy part of a song that listeners remember, usually the title line of the chorus or a riff.
The overall up-and-down shape of a melody.
A song section whose music repeats with new words each time; it tells the story.
The song section that repeats with the same words and music, carrying the main idea and hook.
A short section between verse and chorus that builds tension into the chorus.
A contrasting section heard once, usually before the last choruses; another name for a song's bridge.
The fit between words and music: stressed syllables on strong beats and important words on the hook.
The repeating rhythmic feel of a song: tempo, subdivision and where the accents fall.
Accents on beats 2 and 4 of a 4/4 bar, usually played by the snare drum.
A groove that puts the snare on beat 3 only, so the music feels half as fast as the tempo.
A left-hand piano pattern that breaks a chord into low–high–middle–high (C G E G).
A piano style with bass notes on beats 1 and 3 and mid-range chords on 2 and 4.
The rhythm of down and up strokes a guitarist uses to play chords.
A short repeated instrumental figure, often on the low guitar strings, that carries a song.
A song written as melody, chord symbols and lyrics on one staff.
A metronome played to the musicians while recording so the tempo stays steady.
Software for recording, editing and mixing audio, such as GarageBand, Reaper or Logic.
The space between the loudest peaks of a recording and the 0 dBFS digital ceiling, kept so nothing clips.
